newsitem.title: USA: Two U.S. Democrats to introduce tax loophole bill.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. Democrats to introduce tax loophole bill.

text.p: Two Democratic lawmakers said Monday they will introduce a bill next week to end tax "loopholes" that allow firms and investors to avoid paying taxes on profits and that shift jobs overseas.
Sen. Tom Harkin of Iowa and Rep. Lane Evans of Illinois said their legislation, the "Corporate Welfare Reduction Act," would save the Treasury more than $20 billion over six years.
The "loopholes" and tax breaks they are targeting benefit big oil companies, multinational corporations and foreign investors, the lawmakers said in a statement.

The bill would prevent multinational firms from using transfer pricing rules to lower tax liability, the lawmakers said. "By characterizing certain income as earned abroad even though the sales occurred in the U.S., multinational corporations are able to shift income and avoid paying U.S. tax," the statement said.
The legislation would require foreign citizens to pay capital gains tax on the sale of stock in U.S. firms and pay tax on interest received from U.S. borrowing.
The bill would stop multinational oil and gas companies from claiming foreign tax credits for some of the ordinary costs of doing business in foreign countries, the statement said.

It would end a rule that allows corporations to effectively "pocket" taxable income when sending workers to countries with low or no income tax, the statement said. Americans would still receive a deduction for any income tax incurred while living abroad.
Revenue that would be saved would be earmarked to go toward deficit reduction and export promotion programs for small and mid-size U.S. firms, the lawmakers said.
